hubs.name: Belfast Great Victoria Street railway station

spots.name: SS Nomadic
spots.summary: SS Nomadic is a former tender of the White Star Line, launched on 25 April 1911 at Belfast, that is now on display in Belfast's Titanic Quarter. She was built to transfer passengers and mail to and from the ocean liners RMS Olympic and RMS Titanic.

spots.name: Belfast City Hall
spots.summary: Belfast City Hall is the civic building of Belfast City Council located in Donegall Square, Belfast, Northern Ireland. It faces North and effectively divides the commercial and business areas of the city centre. It is a Grade A listed building.

names.ja: ベルファスト・シティホール

spots.name: HMS Caroline

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: HMS Caroline is a decommissioned C-class light cruiser of the Royal Navy that was the lead ship of her sub-class. Completed in 1914, she saw combat service during the First World War and served as an administrative centre in the Second World War.

spots.name: St Anne's Cathedral, Belfast

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Anne's Cathedral is a Romanesque-style Anglican cathedral in Donegall Street, Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is unusual in serving two separate dioceses. It is the focal point of Belfast's Cathedral Quarter.

photo.author: The original uploader was Stuart at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Shankill Road
spots.summary: The Shankill Road is one of the main roads leading through West Belfast, in Northern Ireland. It runs through the working-class, predominantly loyalist, area known as the Shankill.

spots.name: The Big Fish
spots.summary: The Big Fish, also known as the Salmon of Knowledge, is a printed ceramic mosaic sculpture by John Kindness. The 10-metre-long (33 ft) statue was constructed in 1999 and installed on Donegall Quay in Belfast, Northern Ireland, near the Lagan Lookout and Custom House.

spots.name: Albert Memorial Clock

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Albert Memorial Clock is a clock tower situated at Queen's Square in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It was completed in 1869 and is one of the best known landmarks of Belfast.

spots.name: Ulster Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Ulster Museum, located in the Botanic Gardens in Belfast, has around 8,000 square metres of public display space, featuring material from the collections of fine art and applied art, archaeology, ethnography, treasures from the Spanish Armada, local history, numismatics, industrial archaeology, botany, zoology and geology.

names.ja: アルスター国立博物館

spots.name: Belfast Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Belfast Castle is a mansion located in Cave Hill Country Park in Belfast, Northern Ireland, in a prominent position 400 feet (120 m) above sea level. Its location provides unobstructed views over the City of Belfast and Belfast Lough.

spots.name: Parliament Buildings

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Parliament Buildings, often referred to as Stormont, because of its location in the Stormont Estate area of Belfast, is the seat of the Northern Ireland Assembly, the devolved legislature for Northern Ireland.

names.ja: 政府庁舎 (ベルファスト)

spots.name: Titanic Memorial
spots.summary: The Titanic Memorial in Belfast was erected to commemorate the lives lost in the sinking of the RMS Titanic on 15 April 1912. It was funded by contributions from the public, shipyard workers, and victims' families, and was dedicated in June 1920.

names.es: Monumento conmemorativo del Titanic en Belfast

spots.name: Donegall Square
spots.summary: Donegall Square is a square in the centre of Belfast, Northern Ireland. At its centre is Belfast City Hall, the headquarters of Belfast City Council.

spots.name: Sandy Row
spots.summary: Sandy Row is an inner city area of south Belfast, Northern Ireland, which is predominantly Protestant working-class. In 2018, the population was estimated to be around 4,000. It is a staunchly loyalist area and heartland of the paramilitary Ulster Defence Association (UDA) and Orange Order.

spots.name: Crown Liquor Saloon
spots.summary: The Crown Liquor Saloon, also known as the Crown Bar, is a pub in Great Victoria Street in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Refurbished in 1885, and at least twice since, it is an outstanding example of a Victorian gin palace, and one of Northern Ireland's best-known pubs.

spots.name: HM Prison Belfast
spots.summary: HM Prison Belfast, also known as Crumlin Road Gaol, is a former prison situated on the Crumlin Road in north Belfast, Northern Ireland. Since 1996 it is the only remaining Victorian era former prison in Northern Ireland. It is colloquially known as the Crum.

names.ja: クラムリン通り刑務所

spots.name: Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: Botanic Gardens is a public garden in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

spots.name: Beacon of Hope
spots.summary: The Beacon of Hope, Harmony of Belfast or Thanksgiving Square Beacon is a £300,000 public art metal sculpture by Andy Scott of 19.5 metres high constructed in 2007 in Thanksgiving Square in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

spots.name: Ulster Hall
spots.summary: The Ulster Hall is a concert hall and grade A listed building in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Situated at 34 Bedford Street in Belfast city centre, the hall hosts concerts, classical recitals, craft fairs and political party conferences.

spots.name: St Peter's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Peter's Cathedral, Belfast, is the Catholic cathedral church for the Diocese of Down and Connor, and is therefore the episcopal seat of the Catholic Bishop of Down and Connor. It is located in the Divis Street area of the Falls Road in Belfast, Northern Ireland, and construction began in the 1860s.

photo.author: St_petersbelfast.jpg: Finaghy (talk). The original uploader was Finaghy at Engli

spots.name: Kelly's Cellars
spots.summary: Kelly's Cellars is a pub in Belfast, Northern Ireland, situated at 30 Bank Street in the city centre. Built on 14 March 1720, it is one of the oldest pubs of Belfast.

spots.name: Windsor House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Windsor House was a 23-story, 80 m high-rise building on Bedford Street in Belfast, Northern Ireland. The building was the tallest storeyed building in Northern Ireland before being surpassed by the Obel Tower which stands at 85 metres (279 feet) tall, with 28 floors.

spots.name: Great Victoria Street
spots.summary: Great Victoria Street in Belfast, Northern Ireland, is a major thoroughfare located in the city centre and is one of the important streets used by pedestrians alighting from Belfast Grand Central and walking into shopping streets such as Royal Avenue.

spots.name: Belfast Wheel
spots.summary: The Belfast Wheel was a 60-metre (200 ft) tall transportable Ferris wheel installation in the centre of Belfast, Northern Ireland, in the grounds on the east side of Belfast City Hall. It operated from November 2007 to April 2010.

spots.name: Royal Avenue
spots.summary: Royal Avenue is a street in the heart of Belfast city centre, Northern Ireland. It runs for about 500 metres from the junction with Castle Place and Donegall Place to the junction with Donegall Street. It lies between the Cathedral Quarter and the Smithfield and Union Quarter of the city.

spots.name: Milltown Cemetery
spots.summary: Milltown Cemetery is a cemetery in west Belfast, Northern Ireland. It lies within the townland of Ballymurphy, between the Falls Road and the M1 motorway.

spots.name: Belfast Cenotaph
spots.summary: The Belfast Cenotaph is a war memorial in Belfast, Northern Ireland, in Donegall Square West, to the west of Belfast City Hall. Like the City Hall, it was designed by Sir Alfred Brumwell Thomas. The cenotaph was unveiled in 1929. It became a Grade A listed building in 1984.

spots.name: St George's Church, Belfast

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. George's Church, Belfast is a Church of Ireland church located on High Street in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is the oldest Church of Ireland church in Belfast. It was designed by Irish architect, John Bowden, and opened in 1816. Major refurbishment work was completed in June 2000.

spots.name: St George's Market

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: St George's Market is the last surviving Victorian covered market in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is located on May Street, close to the River Lagan and the Waterfront Hall. Belfast Corporation commissioned the building of St George's Market, which was built in three phases between 1890 and 1896.

names.ja: セント・ジョージ・マーケット

spots.name: Linen Hall Library

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Linen Hall Library is located at 17 Donegall Square North, Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is the oldest library in Belfast and the last subscribing library in Northern Ireland.

spots.name: Giant's Ring

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Giant's Ring is a henge monument at Ballynahatty, near Shaw's Bridge, Belfast, Northern Ireland. The site is a State Care Historic Monument and also a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

spots.name: Friar's Bush Graveyard
spots.summary: Friar's Bush Graveyard is the oldest Christian burial site in the city of Belfast in Northern Ireland. A mound in the graveyard is believed to date from the Neolithic period. It is located on the Stranmillis Road in South Belfast. It had a B1 listed status.

spots.name: Queen's Bridge
spots.summary: Queen's Bridge is a B+ listed Victorian stone arch bridge in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It opened to traffic in 1843 and is named after Queen Victoria.

spots.name: Belfast Zoo
spots.summary: Belfast Zoological Gardens is a zoo in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is in a relatively secluded location on the northeastern slope of Cavehill, overlooking Belfast's Antrim Road. Opened in 1934, it is the second-oldest zoo in Ireland, after Dublin Zoo, which opened in 1831.

spots.name: Spirit of Belfast
spots.summary: The Spirit of Belfast is a public art sculpture by Dan George in Belfast, Northern Ireland. The sculpture was unveiled on 25 September 2009 after a series of delays and is located on Arthur Square, close to the main point of access to Victoria Square. The sculpture is constructed of steel and cost £200,000.

spots.name: RISE
spots.summary: RISE is the official name given to the public art sculpture located at Broadway Roundabout in Belfast, Northern Ireland. However, it has been given unofficial, colloquial titles such as the "Balls of the Falls", "the Testes on the Westes" and "the Westicles".

spots.name: Queen Elizabeth Bridge
spots.summary: Queen Elizabeth Bridge is a bridge over the River Lagan in Belfast, Northern Ireland, which opened in 1966.

names.ja: クイーンエリザベス橋

spots.name: Dargan Bridge, Belfast
spots.summary: Dargan Bridge is a railway bridge which crosses the River Lagan in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Opened in 1994, it directly connected the Dublin and Bangor lines with the lines to Larne and Derry for the first time.

spots.name: North Street Arcade
spots.summary: The North Street Arcade is a 1930s Art Deco shopping arcade in the Cathedral Quarter of Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is the only example of a shopping arcade from this decade in Northern Ireland, and is one of only a handful left in the whole of Ireland or the UK.

spots.name: Monument to the Unknown Woman Worker
spots.summary: The Monument to the Unknown Woman Worker is a 1992 sculpture by Louise Walsh in Belfast, Northern Ireland, located on Great Victoria Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the Unknown Woman Worker

names.es: Monumento a la mujer trabajadora desconocida

spots.name: Golden Mile
spots.summary: The Golden Mile is the name given to the stretch of Dublin Road, Great Victoria Street, Bradbury Place and University Road between the City Hall and the university area in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

spots.name: Assembly Rooms
spots.summary: The Assembly Rooms is a Grade B1 listed building in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It was built, as the single-storey Exchange, in 1769 by Arthur Chichester, 1st Marquess of Donegall. The Marquess expanded to a second floor in 1776 and the building came to be known by its current name.

spots.name: Northern Ireland War Memorial

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Northern Ireland War Memorial also called NI War Memorial and War Memorial was opened in 2007 in Talbot Street, Belfast, Northern Ireland. It replaced an earlier building called Memorial House which was located in Waring Street on a site which was bombed during the Blitz in 1941.

spots.name: St Malachy's Church, Belfast

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Malachy's Church is a Catholic church in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is located in Alfred Street, a short distance from Belfast City Hall, although it precedes that building by over 60 years.

spots.name: Garden of Remembrance
spots.summary: The Garden of Remembrance is a memorial garden in Belfast, Northern Ireland, dedicated to the Irish Republican Army members killed during The Troubles, as well as civilians and deceased ex-prisoners. It is located on the Falls Road, which has historically been a predominantly Irish Republican area during the conflict.

spots.name: Albert Bridge, Belfast
spots.summary: Albert Bridge is a bridge in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Its three flat arches span the River Lagan. It was completed in 1890 by Belfast city surveyor J C Bretland and is named after Prince Albert Victor. It is located close to the city centre between East Bridge Street and the Albertbridge Road.

spots.name: Belfast Central Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Belfast Central Library is a public library in Royal Avenue, Belfast, Northern Ireland. Opened in 1888, it was one of the first major public library buildings in Ireland.

spots.name: The Calling
spots.summary: The Calling is an outdoor sculpture by Paddy McCann located in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Located at the junction of Gordon Street and Dunbar Junction, it consists of a bright red stylised male human figure calling into the distance while standing on an ordinary chair atop an extended piston-like arm.

spots.name: Clonard Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Clonard Monastery is a Catholic church located off the Falls Road in Belfast, Northern Ireland, and home to a community of the Redemptorists religious order.

spots.name: Queen's Arcade, Belfast
spots.summary: Queen's Arcade is a Grade B1 listed Victorian shopping arcade in the centre of Belfast, Northern Ireland. Extending between Donegall Place and Fountain Street, it is the last remaining Victorian shopping arcade in the city.

spots.name: Northern Bank Headquarters
spots.summary: The Northern Bank Headquarters in Belfast is the head office of Danske Bank in Northern Ireland after being acquired by Danske Bank in 2005. It is located in Donegall Square West and was the location of the infamous Northern Bank robbery which is among the largest bank robberies in United Kingdom history.

spots.name: Irish Republican History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Eileen Hickey Irish Republican History Museum, is a museum in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It was established in 2007 after years of campaigning by Eileen Hickey, who collected the exhibits.

spots.name: Windsor Park
spots.summary: The National Football Stadium at Windsor Park, more commonly known as Windsor Park, is a football stadium in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

spots.name: Boyne Bridge
spots.summary: The Boyne Bridge was a bridge in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It was built in 1863 over the Belfast–Lisburn railway line, and was rebuilt in 1936. It was scheduled for demolition starting on 12 October 2024, to be replaced by a road at ground level, which is set to take one year to complete.

spots.name: Elmwood Hall
spots.summary: Elmwood Hall is a concert hall and former Presbyterian church on University Road in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is situated opposite Queen's University Belfast.

spots.name: St Patrick's Church, Belfast

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Patrick's Church, Belfast is a Catholic church located in the Donegall Street area of Belfast, Northern Ireland. It is built in the Romanesque Revival style, with a four-stage tower and spire rising from the front west elevation. The first church opened on the site in 1815, while the current building opened in 1877.

spots.name: Old Town Hall, Belfast
spots.summary: The Old Town Hall is a municipal structure in Victoria Street, Belfast, Northern Ireland. The structure, which has most recently been used as courthouse, is a Grade B1 listed building.

spots.name: Lagan Viaduct
spots.summary: Lagan Railway Bridge is a railway and pedestrian bridge across the River Lagan in Belfast, slightly north of Belfast Central railway station. The next bridge upstream is the Albert Bridge, whilst the next downstream is Queen's Bridge.

spots.name: Shaw's Bridge
spots.summary: Shaw's Bridge is the name given to two adjacent bridges across the River Lagan in Belfast, Northern Ireland. The older of the bridges is a historic stone arched bridge, which is open to cyclists and pedestrians. The new bridge is a concrete bridge which carries the A55 road.

spots.name: Kitchen Bar
spots.summary: The Kitchen Bar is a pub in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It dates back to 1859 but on 30 July 2004, the original building was demolished to make way for Victoria Square, a shopping centre. The original building was a women's boardinghouse prior to its use as a pub.

spots.name: Water Office, Belfast
spots.summary: The Water Office is a former warehouse at 1 Donegall Square in Belfast, Northern Ireland, that is listed by the Department for Communities (DfC), part of the Northern Ireland Executive, at grade B1, citing both "Historic Interest" and "Architectural Interest".

spots.name: Titanic Belfast
spots.summary: For a century this was the "T-word" in Belfast, even more than the Troubles, an unwelcome reminder of a catastrophe reflecting badly on the city. This exhibition, opened in 2012 in a striking modern building, has revitalised a whole city quarter and rescued RMS Titanic as a source of local pride, for its construction and its crew. You progress through the metal-bashing boomtown of Victorian and Ed

spots.name: Queen's University

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: August red-brick Victorian building in Tudor style modelled on Magdalen College Oxford, with extensive grounds. On University Square note the fine Union Theological College: the Northern Ireland Parliament spent its early years here until Stormont was ready in 1932.

spots.name: Titanic Distillery and Pump House

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: Impressive dry dock where the ship was launched, and the pump house which drained and flooded the dock. The pump house has been converted into a whiskey distillery which offers regular tours and tastings.

spots.name: W5

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed

spots.summary: Interactive science museum aimed at younger children. Booking essential.

spots.name: Cultúrlann McAdam Ó Fiaich

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The hub of Irish language activities in Belfast. It's a cultural centre with visitor information, art, trad music, a cafe and a bookshop. They put on regular Irish language classes, from beginners to advanced.

spots.name: Robinsons Bar

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: Trad "long" pub, established 1895. The saloon (front end off GVS) is decorated with Titanic memorabilia, this is the area for a quiet pint. Head to the first floor bistro for food, served until 9PM. The back bar is Fibber Magees, which you can also enter via the alley behind Travelodge: this has trad music every night.

spots.name: The John Hewitt

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This pub is run by Boundary Brewing based in East Belfast. 19 taps of craft beer as well as a great selection of cans and bottles in the fridge. Franky's Lasangeria also operates in here selling great portions of chicken parm and deep-fried lasagne bites.

spots.name: Duke of York

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The main Duke of York bar is a classic mirrored beer hall, Harp Bar is a trad saloon with live music, The New Orpheus is its swish extension, The Friend at Hand is the whiskey collection, and The Dark Horse is their events venue.

spots.name: Sunflower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lively pub, don't let the security cage put you off , inside is a very welcoming pub with great craft beers on tap and some of the cheapest pints in the city centre.

spots.name: Limelight

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Standard pub early evening, then late night there are four music and club areas: Katy's the main bar, Limelight 1 and 2, and the rooftop Rock Garden.

spots.name: Morning Star

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Grand alehouse since 1810. Downstairs is a traditional bar whilst upstairs is a food orientated lounge specialising in steaks and whiskey.

spots.name: McHugh's

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: In a building of 1711, with a 100-seat restaurant, a basement bar offering live entertainment and the main gallery. Often has trad music.

spots.name: Bright's Restaurant
spots.summary: Old style breakfast and lunch, and traditional ambiance right down to the biddy brushing under your table as you're trying to eat.

spots.name: Whites Tavern

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Founded in 1630 and probably Belfast's oldest pub. Cosy bar with live music on Friday nights, the Oyster Rooms are the bistro.

spots.name: Darcy's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Large servings of Belfast cuisine in an old-fashioned candlelit ambiance. Excellent vegan/vegetarian menu.

spots.name: Little Wing Pizzeria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Slick friendly place serves pizza Napoli-style. Also has branches on Lisburn Rd and Upper Newtownards Rd.

spots.name: Doorsteps

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Stonking great sandwiches (hence the name) and trad meals, you'll need a hearty appetite.

spots.name: Scalini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent pizzeria and trattoria near QUB, they make sure you realise they're Italian.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Reliably good place, especially good value for lunch and dim sum.

spots.summary: Good Indian restaurant, the lunchtime deals are great value.

spots.summary: City centre pub in the shopping arcade does good grills.

spots.summary: Michelin-starred restaurant, reservations essential.

spots.summary: Reliable chain pub, good value food and drink.
